clue.text: Predict toll-free trips

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters of the preceding word fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone forecasts free passage on a toll road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' looks like journeys but is a verb signalling the letters of 'toll-free' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict is to say in advance what will happen, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Music group releases record — Let It Be

indicators.note: releases means the group lets go of the piece named next, which drops out of its letters

parts.note: a septet is a group of seven musicians
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A band puts out the Beatles single Let It Be.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface names the Beatles song; the definition is the proofreader's instruction to leave text as it was.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin mark tells a printer to ignore a correction, literally 'let it stand'.

clue.text: Magistrates rise to defend a marine boss

indicators.note: to defend is to surround something protectively, so one piece goes around the other
in a down clue rising means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: doges were the chief magistrates of Venice and Genoa

explanation.surface: Judges get up to protect an admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon or Neptune is a deity ruling over the ocean, a boss of the sea.

clue.text: German city church makes one concentrate

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church in a German town helps someone focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concentrate' looks like a verb but is a noun: an extract.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract boiled down to its strongest form is a concentrate, as with vanilla.

clue.text: Helping a person to keep dry

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a being is a living person
TT means teetotal, i.e. not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: Assisting someone to stay off the booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetting is assisting, usually in wrongdoing; helping is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Name place for 50 in correspondence

indicators.note: one thing put for another replaces it, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: a relation between things is a correspondence
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to place is to put

explanation.surface: Instructions for where to write a number in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' suggests letters, but here it means a connection or link between things.
explanation.definitionFit: A good name means standing in public esteem, as in 'make a name for yourself'.

clue.text: Cutter travelled north to save Italian

indicators.note: to save is to keep safe inside, so one piece holds the other
in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: A boat went north to rescue an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: A cutter is also a small ship, matching 'travelled north'; here it is someone who trims text or film.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or newspaper editor cuts material, so cutter describes the job.

clue.text: Female soldiers lock castle

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Women soldiers secure a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a stronghold, as is a fortified building of this kind.

clue.text: Business leader does, perhaps, return stock

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
return means the word is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: does are female deer, an example of the group

explanation.surface: A company boss gives back shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb; it is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock means lineage or strain of animals, a synonym for a line of descent.

clue.text: Behind main square

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can stand for square

explanation.surface: Something lies to the rear of the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a preposition; it is the noun for one's bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Your backside is the part you sit on, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Lancaster's collecting new rate for relatives

indicators.note: collecting means gathering something up inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: John of Gaunt was Duke of Lancaster, so Lancaster is Gaunt, and 's adds S

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A Lancaster company charges a new rate to family members.
explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster, was a son of Edward III; 'Lancaster' as a name for him is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Your parents' aunts are family members two generations up.

clue.text: Let Liberal relax with daughter

parts.note: to ease is to relax or loosen

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician lets his daughter unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like 'allow'; it is the past tense of renting out property.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat that has been let has been rented out to a tenant under a contract.

clue.text: Strip for these gaunt ducks

parts.note: gaunt means very thin
to duck is to dip quickly under water

explanation.surface: A thin bird sheds its feathers for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' looks like birds but is a verb, plunges; the definition describes undressing before a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathers who swim naked must first take off their clothes for such outings.

clue.text: Courtesy of chief rival wounded close to Burgundy

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged, so the letters are broken into a new order
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A chief rival is hurt near the Burgundy region, a courtesy gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant politeness, originally the code of knights, is courtesy.

clue.text: Fall over in middle of breezy Oval

indicators.note: in places one piece within another
the middle of a word is its central letters
over means turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a spill is a fall

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles in the middle of a windy cricket ground, the Oval.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, which steers away from the geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This geometric curve is the shape of an elongated circle, i.e. an oval.

clue.text: Stalls stocking Times replacements

indicators.note: stocking means holding goods inside, so one piece is filled with the other

parts.note: stands are market stalls
by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Market stalls carry copies of the Times as substitutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Understudies or reserves who can step in are substitutes ready to take over.

clue.text: Opposed to profits at banks

indicators.note: banks surround a river, so the first piece forms the edges around the second

parts.note: gains are profits

explanation.surface: Someone objects to the profits of banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like the lenders but is a verb: A and T form the banks around the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is to oppose it, a simple prepositional equivalent.

clue.text: Most daft stories appear in random list

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be found inside it
random means put into no particular order, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: lies are stories, as in 'telling stories'

explanation.surface: The silliest tales show up in a haphazard list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'random' shuffles the letters of 'list', and the stories sit inside that shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of foolish, most daft, is the same as most silly.

clue.text: Notice about Queen Victoria's delivery in court

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes around the rest

parts.note: to see is to notice
R is for Regina, Latin for queen
Vic is a short form of Victoria

explanation.surface: A legal notice concerning Queen Victoria is delivered in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'court' is a tennis court; 'delivery' is the serve that starts a point.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the shot that starts each point is delivered by the server.

clue.text: Garden rubbish primarily encourages sloth, maybe

parts.note: Eden is the Garden of Eden
tat is cheap rubbish

indicators.note: primarily means first, so take the opening letter

explanation.surface: Junk in the garden makes people lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloth' suggests idleness, a deadly sin; it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloths, anteaters and armadillos are toothless or nearly so, so a sloth is an example.

clue.text: Duke hates novel offering more than one ending

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: An aristocrat dislikes a book with alternative endings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the end of life: each one is an ending, so several are more than one.

clue.text: The Spanish fly around conflict

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: Spanish fly is mentioned around a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish fly' is a supposed aphrodisiac; split, it gives two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle can be a confused fight or quarrel, as in 'get into a tangle with'.

clue.text: Broadcast unsettled John

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: thrown means disconcerted or unsettled

explanation.surface: A broadcast upset someone named John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name; it is American slang for a lavatory, which is humorously called the royal seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The toilet is humorously the seat of power, and john is slang for it.

clue.text: Passed front of harbour, also English port

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: and means also
Dover is a Channel port in Kent

explanation.surface: A ship sailed by a harbour and an English port.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something to someone is to give it over to them.

clue.text: What I've got here contributes to ancient history

indicators.note: contributes to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something being shown adds to the study of ancient history.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrative pointing at the item close at hand, as in 'look at what I have here'.

clue.text: Constant regret follows Tory leader

indicators.note: follows places the regret after the leader piece
the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Remorse that is ever present trails the Conservative leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant in the sense of loyal and faithful, as a steadfast friend is.

clue.text: Contented double parking in grass

indicators.note: in places the doubled piece within the other

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: double means the letter appears twice

parts.note: P is the map sign for parking

explanation.surface: Someone is satisfied with twice the parking on the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Content and pleased mean satisfied, simple synonyms.

clue.text: Tory hunt victory

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, i.e. Tory
a quest is a hunt or search

explanation.surface: A Conservative chase ends in a win.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning by force or effort is a triumph, a near synonym.
